title: What is a Co-op?
description: How cooperatives work and why CCD is member-owned and governed.
heroBody: A cooperative is an autonomous association of people united voluntarily to meet common economic, social, and cultural needs through a jointly-owned, democratically-controlled enterprise.
heroAlt: Together We Can Do Great Things mural

steps.title: Members join
steps.body: Residents, businesses, and supporters pay dues that fund the shared work of the co-op.

steps.title: Members govern
steps.body: Voting members each get one vote. Major decisions come back to the membership.

steps.title: Members share benefits
steps.body: Tool access, service discounts, markets, and neighborhood improvements stay local.

sections.title: The cooperative principles.
sections.body: CCD follows the internationally recognized cooperative principles, adapted for Irvington and Baltimore's 21229.

cards.title: Voluntary & open membership
cards.body: Open to all who can use the co-op's services and accept the responsibilities of membership.

cards.title: Democratic member control
cards.body: One member, one vote. Members set direction and hold leadership accountable.

cards.title: Member economic participation
cards.body: Members contribute dues and share in the benefits the co-op creates.

cards.title: Autonomy & independence
cards.body: CCD is a self-help organization controlled by its members.

cards.title: Education & training
cards.body: The co-op invests in members so they can contribute to its development.

cards.title: Concern for community
cards.body: CCD works for the sustainable development of Irvington and the wider 21229.

sections.title: This is your co-op. Own a piece of it.
sections.body: Membership turns support into governance, and dues into visible community benefit.
